requested_parts: Pods selected in a four-player game.
Pod distribution and orientation.
Tokens starting in the Intruder bag.
answers.answer: 1. Select 3 Escape Pods. 2. Put the lowest-numbered in Section A, next in Section B, then alternate A/B; all start Locked side up. 3. The bag has 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, and 3 Adults plus 1 additional Adult per player: 7 Adults at four players.
answers.evidence: 1. “Take randomly chosen Escape Pod tokens: 2 pods for 1–2 players, 3 for 3–4 players, 4 for 5 players.” Inference: four players means 3 Pods. 2. “Place the lowest-numbered pod in Section ‘A’, the next (in numerical order) in Section ‘B’, then alternate A/B. All pods start with their Locked side face up.” 3. “Put these Intruder tokens in the Intruder bag: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player.” Inference: 3 + 4 = 7 Adults.

requested_parts: Objective filtering and dealing.
When an Objective is chosen and what happens to the rejected card.
Whether Eggs trigger that choice.
answers.answer: 1. Remove cards requiring more than P players from both Objective decks; separately shuffle and deal each player 1 Corporate and 1 Personal Objective, kept hidden. 2. At the First Encounter, each player immediately chooses 1 of their 2 Objectives; remove the other face down, unseen by anyone. 3. Eggs do not trigger the choice; the first Intruder miniature appearing does, and Eggs are not Intruders.
answers.evidence: 1. “Let P be the actual number of players in this game. Remove from both Objective decks (Corporate and Personal) every card requiring more than P players. Shuffle the two decks separately and deal each player 1 Corporate and 1 Personal Objective card, kept hidden.” 2. “First Encounter: the first time an Intruder miniature (of any type) appears on the board, every player immediately chooses 1 of their 2 Objective cards and removes the other from the game face down (unseen by anyone — players may never look at others' removed Objectives). Then the triggering Encounter is resolved.” 3. “Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this.”

requested_parts: What is discarded to pay a cost-2 Action card with the stated hand.
Whether Contamination can substitute for payment.
How OR choices work.
answers.answer: 1. Discard the played card and the 2 other Action cards, 3 Action cards total; keep both Contamination cards. 2. Contamination cards cannot pay any Action cost. 3. Choose one of the card's sections separated by OR.
answers.evidence: 1. “For an Action card, also discard the card you play: printed cost n requires n + 1 Action cards in total.” “Each Character has a partially unique deck of 10 Action cards. To use one, discard that card face up and pay its cost by discarding the required number of additional Action cards.” Inference: cost 2 requires the played card plus two other Action cards, exactly the three Action cards stated. 2. “Contamination cards are not Action cards: they can never be discarded to pay any Action cost.” 3. “If a card has two sections separated by ‘OR,’ choose one.”

requested_parts: Timing of the Fire wound after one Action and passing.
Whether the Character may take more normal Actions this Player Phase.
Whether they may discard hand cards when passing.
Whether later players' rounds cause them more Fire wounds.
answers.answer: 1. Taking only one Action means the Character must pass; they take 1 Light Wound at the end of their own passing round. 2. They cannot take further normal Actions in this Player Phase (Interruption remains permitted). 3. At the moment of passing they may discard any number of hand cards. 4. No; later players' rounds cause no additional Fire wound to them that turn.
answers.evidence: 1. “If you perform only 1 Action instead of two, you must pass.” “A Character who ends their round in a Room with a Fire marker suffers 1 Light Wound (every round; only after finishing their own round — passing players take it once at the end of their round and no more that turn).” 2. “Normal Actions | You cannot take further normal Actions; Interruption remains permitted as below.” 3. “Hand cards | At the moment you pass, you may discard any number of cards from your hand.” 4. “Fire in your Room | Take 1 Light Wound at the end of your own passing round. Later players' rounds do not give you further Fire wounds that turn.”

requested_parts: Reveal of the unexplored Room and setting its Item Counter.
Resolution and destination of the Exploration token.
When Movement Noise is rolled, including Silence/Danger.
Effect of an occupied destination on Movement Noise.
answers.answer: 1. Flip the unexplored tile face up. For a normal Room tile, orient the Exploration token's number to the board's Item Counter symbol; the Nest and Room Covered With Slime have no Item count. 2. Resolve the token effect (Silence, Danger, Slime, Fire, Malfunction, or Doors; Doors go in the Corridor used to enter), then remove the token from the game into the box. 3. Silence or Danger replaces the Movement Noise roll; otherwise roll only if the destination is empty. 4. If a Character or Intruder is already there, do not roll Movement Noise.
answers.evidence: 1. “After entering a Room: (1) if the Room tile was unexplored (face down), flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return that token to the box (removed from the game); (2) apply the Movement Noise rule.” “Item Counter: the Nest and Room Covered With Slime get no Item count. For other Room tiles, rotate the tile until the Exploration token's number faces the Item Counter symbol printed on the board next to the slot.” 2. “Resolve the effect: Silence — no Movement Noise roll. Nothing happens. If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve ‘Danger’ instead. Danger — no Movement Noise roll. Move ALL eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into this Room (eligible means not in Combat with any Character). If there are none eligible, place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to this Room that lacks one, counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance. Slime — place a Slime (Status) marker on your Character board. Fire — place a Fire marker in this Room. Malfunction — place a Malfunction marker in this Room. Doors — place a Door token in the Corridor by which you entered.” “After resolving an Exploration token, remove it from the game into the box; it does not return to a supply or stay on the Room (each is resolved only once, on first entry).” 3. “A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward.” “Otherwise, perform the ordinary Noise roll if the destination is empty (no Characters, no Intruders).” 4. “If anyone — Character or Intruder — is already there, do NOT roll for Movement Noise.”

requested_parts: Careful Movement's cost and what it replaces.
When Careful Movement is forbidden.
Closed Door and stopping-in-Corridor restrictions.
answers.answer: 1. It costs 2 Action cards, replaces the after-movement Noise roll with placing a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination, and also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results with that placement. 2. It is forbidden in Combat and if all Corridors connected to the destination already have Noise markers. 3. It follows normal movement restrictions, so a Closed Door blocks passage; miniatures may never stop in Corridors.
answers.evidence: 1. “Careful Movement (cost 2) — follows normal Movement restrictions, including Closed Doors blocking passage; but instead of a Noise roll after moving, place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the Room you enter. You cannot Carefully Move if all Corridors connected to the destination already hold Noise markers, and you cannot use it while in Combat. The FAQ clarifies that Careful Movement also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results with its chosen Noise placement; Reconnaissance cancels those automatic results too.” 3. “Characters and Intruders may only occupy Rooms (Special Rooms — Hibernatorium, Cockpit, Engines — count as Rooms; Escape Pod tokens are the only exception for Characters). Corridors connect Rooms; no one may ever stop in a Corridor.” “Two Rooms are neighboring when directly connected by 1 Corridor. A Closed Door blocks the ‘neighboring’ status for players' Movement.”

requested_parts: Effect of trying to place Noise where a marker already exists, including Technical Corridors.
Noise removal at Encounter start.
Drawn token placement and return handling.
Surprise Attack comparison and whether Contamination counts.
answers.answer: 1. A Corridor holds at most 1 Noise marker; attempting to place another resolves an Encounter. A marker on the shared Technical Corridors space counts for every Technical Corridors Entrance. 2. Discard all Noise markers from all Corridors connected to the Encounter Room, including Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance. 3. Draw an Intruder token; keep a non-Blank token aside outside the bag (not immediately returned) and place its matching miniature in the Room. 4. Compare the token number to all cards in the triggering player's hand, counting Action and Contamination cards. Fewer cards than the number causes a Surprise Attack against that Character; equal or more causes no attack.
answers.evidence: 1. “Result 1, 2, 3, or 4: place a Noise marker in the Corridor with that number connected to the Room you entered (counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance). A Corridor may never hold more than 1 Noise marker — if instructed to place a marker where one already is, resolve an Encounter instead.” “If a Noise marker's number leads to a Technical Corridors Entrance, place the marker on the Technical Corridors space. A Noise marker there is treated as if it were in every Technical Corridors Entrance on the whole board. The 1-marker limit applies: placing a second one there resolves an Encounter instead.” 2. “Resolve: 1. Discard ALL Noise markers from all Corridors connected to the Room (including Technical Corridors if there's an Entrance).” 3. “Draw 1 Intruder token from the bag (symbol on one side, number on the other). Keep a non-Blank token aside outside the bag; it is not immediately returned. A Blank follows its separate return procedure below.” “Place the matching Intruder miniature in the Room.” 4. “Compare the token's number to the number of cards in the triggering player's hand (Action AND Contamination cards both count). Fewer cards than the number → Surprise Attack (an Intruder Attack against that Character). Equal or more → nothing happens.”

requested_parts: Danger with eligible neighboring Intruders and with none eligible.
Whether moving into a Character's Room is an Encounter.
Slime's effect on Silence.
answers.answer: 1. Move all eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into the Room; an eligible Intruder is not in Combat with any Character. If none are eligible, place Noise in each connected Corridor that lacks a marker, including Technical Corridors when applicable. 2. No: merely moving into a Room with a Character is not an Encounter; they are simply in Combat. 3. Slime makes Silence resolve as Danger.
answers.evidence: 1. “Danger — no Movement Noise roll. Move ALL eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into this Room (eligible means not in Combat with any Character). If there are none eligible, place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to this Room that lacks one, counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance.” 2. “An Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is NOT an Encounter (they are simply in Combat).” 3. “Silence — no Movement Noise roll. Nothing happens. If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve ‘Danger’ instead.”

requested_parts: Noise and Blank handling during an Encounter.
When an Adult is added during a Blank Encounter.
Blank handling during bag development.
answers.answer: 1. Place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to the Room; return the Blank token to the bag, and no miniature appears. 2. Add 1 Adult token only if the Blank was the last token in the bag and an Adult is available. 3. In bag development, add an Adult if one is available (otherwise nothing happens), then return Blank to the bag.
answers.evidence: 1. “Blank token in an Encounter: place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room. If the Blank was the LAST token in the bag: add 1 Adult token to the bag (if any are available; otherwise nothing). Return the Blank token to the bag. The Encounter ends (no miniature appears).” 2. The quoted rule expressly makes this addition conditional on the Blank being the last token in the bag and an Adult being available. 3. “Blank — add 1 Adult Intruder token to the bag (if none are available, nothing happens). Return the Blank token to the bag.”

requested_parts: Where the Intruders end and what happens to the Closed Door.
Whether a Destroyed Door can be closed later.
Whether a Closed Door blocks a Noise-triggered Intruder appearance.
answers.answer: 1. Both Intruders stay in their original Room, and the Door is destroyed. When several Intruders move from that Room through the same Closed Door, they destroy it simultaneously and all stay put. 2. Only the Plasma Torch can close a Destroyed Door. 3. No; an Intruder arriving through that Corridor due to a Noise roll appears regardless of the Closed Door.
answers.evidence: 1. “Closed = standing token: blocks Character and Intruder movement (and Grenade throws). An Intruder trying to move through a Closed Door does not move — it destroys the Door instead (several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put). Destroyed = lying token: movement allowed — only the Plasma Torch Item can Close a Destroyed Door.” 2. “Destroyed = lying token: movement allowed — only the Plasma Torch Item can Close a Destroyed Door. Other Door-closing effects cannot Close it.” 3. “If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door.”

requested_parts: What happens to the Intruder miniature, injuries, token, and Noise when it moves into Technical Corridors.
Whether Characters or Doors may normally use Technical Corridors.
answers.answer: 1. The Intruder disappears into the ducts: remove its miniature from the board, discard all its Injury markers, and return its token to the Intruder bag. The Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space remains. 2. Characters cannot use Technical Corridors except through the Mechanic's Technical Corridors Action card or Technical Corridor Plans Item; Door tokens can never be placed there.
answers.evidence: 1. “If an Intruder moves to a Technical Corridors Entrance, it disappears into the ducts: discard all its Injury markers, return its token to the Intruder bag, and remove its miniature from the board. A Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space is NOT removed by this.” 2. “Some Rooms have Technical Corridors Entrances, all linked to the single Technical Corridors space. Characters can never use them (the only exceptions: the Mechanic's ‘Technical Corridors’ Action card and the ‘Technical Corridor Plans’ Item card).” “Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.”

requested_parts: Action-card cost, Ammo cost, and target location for Shoot versus Melee.
Melee's Contamination draw and destination.
What happens on a miss for each Action.
How the two-hit result is resolved for each Action.
answers.answer: 1. Shoot costs 1 Action card plus 1 Ammo and targets one Intruder in your Room with a Weapon in Hand. Melee costs 1 Action card and targets one Intruder in your Room. 2. Melee draws 1 Contamination card and places it on top of your Action discard pile. 3. An ordinary Shoot miss causes 0 Injury and no Wound to the shooter; a Melee miss causes 0 Injury and 1 Serious Wound to the attacker. 4. The double-hit result deals 2 Injuries to any Intruder with Shoot before Weapon modifiers, while Melee treats two hits as one and deals 1 Injury.
answers.evidence: 1. “Shoot (cost 1): requires a Weapon in Hand with at least 1 Ammo. (1) Choose a Weapon and 1 target Intruder in your Room; (2) discard 1 Ammo from the Weapon card; (3) roll the Combat die.” “Melee Attack (cost 1): (1) draw 1 Contamination card and put it on top of your Action discard pile; (2) choose 1 target Intruder in your Room; (3) roll the Combat die.” 2. “When a Character ‘gets a Contamination card,’ draw it from the Contamination deck and place it on top of their Action discard pile.” 3. “Ordinary attack misses: a Shoot miss deals 0 Injuries to the target and causes no Wound to the shooter. A Melee miss deals 0 Injuries and causes 1 Serious Wound to the attacker.” 4. “Double-hit symbol | 2 Injuries to any Intruder type before Weapon modifiers | 1 Injury to any Intruder type.” “Results mirror Shooting with two changes: any miss also inflicts 1 Serious Wound on your Character, and the 2-Injury result deals only 1 Injury (in melee, rolls of 2 Hits are treated as 1 Hit).”

requested_parts: How Larva, Adult, and Queen Injury Effects are checked after damage.
When a Carcass is placed.
What happens if a Queen check shows a Retreat arrow.
answers.answer: 1. Check current total Injuries. A Larva dies from 1 Injury. For an Adult, draw 1 Intruder Attack card and compare its blood value with total Injuries: blood value less than or equal to Injuries kills it. For a Queen, draw 2 Attack cards and sum their blood values; a sum less than or equal to Injuries kills it. 2. A dead Adult or Queen leaves a Carcass in the Room; a Larva leaves none. 3. If either card in the Queen's two-card check has a Retreat arrow, resolve retreat instead of a numeric death/endurance result: draw an Event card and move the Queen through the Corridor number in its Intruder movement section, then discard that Event card.
answers.evidence: 1. “Intruder Injuries and death: after any Injuries, put that many Injury markers on the Intruder's base and check its Injury Effect. Compare current total Injuries, not just the latest hit.” “Larva | 1 Injury kills | Remove miniature; no Carcass” “Adult | Draw 1 Intruder Attack card; use only its blood value. Blood ≤ Injuries kills; higher means alive.” “Queen | Draw 2 Attack cards and sum blood values. Sum ≤ Injuries kills; higher means alive.” 2. The Injury Effect table states for Adult: “Remove miniature; place Carcass in Room”; for Queen: “Remove miniature; place Carcass in Room”; and for Larva: “Remove miniature; no Carcass.” 3. “Intruder Retreat — move via an Event card: during an Injury Effect check, if any drawn card's blood icon contains the Retreat arrow, resolve retreat instead of a numerical endurance/death result. The Intruder flees: draw an Event card and move the Intruder through the Corridor whose number appears in that card's Intruder movement section, then discard that Event card. The Queen and Breeders retreat if EITHER of their 2 drawn cards shows the Retreat symbol.”

requested_parts: When the Escape attacks happen and their order.
Who is targeted by those Escape attacks.
What happens if the Character dies.
What happens after surviving to an empty unexplored Room.
answers.answer: 1. Before moving, resolve one separate Intruder Attack for each of the two Intruders, in size order from larger to smaller: Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva. 2. Escape attacks target the escaper. 3. If the Character dies, their Corpse stays in the Room they tried to Escape from. 4. If they survive, complete the move to the neighboring Room; reveal and resolve its unexplored tile and Exploration token, then perform the normal Movement Noise procedure because the destination was empty (unless the Exploration result itself replaces that roll, as with Silence or Danger).
answers.evidence: 1. “Character Escape: to leave a Room containing Intruders, perform a Movement Action (cost 1) to a neighboring Room (explored or unexplored). BEFORE moving, resolve an Intruder Attack — one separate Attack per Intruder in the Room, starting with the larger ones (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva; FAQ Rules 5).” 2. “A Surprise Attack targets the Character who triggered the Encounter; an Escape attack targets the escaper.” 3. “If you die, your Corpse stays in the Room you tried to Escape from.” 4. “If you survive, complete the move (Noise roll if the destination is empty; explore normally if unexplored).” “After entering a Room: (1) if the Room tile was unexplored (face down), flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return that token to the box (removed from the game); (2) apply the Movement Noise rule.” “A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward.”

requested_parts: How an ordinary Attack target is chosen when multiple Characters are present and how ties are broken.
How a hit is determined for non-Larva Intruders.
What changes for a Larva and where its Contamination card goes.
answers.answer: 1. The Intruder targets the Character whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand; on a tie, target the First Player, or the next player in turn order. 2. For non-Larvae, draw 1 Intruder Attack card; a matching attacking-Intruder symbol means resolve the effect, and a nonmatching symbol means the attack misses. Ignore the blood icon during attacks. 3. A Larva draws no Attack card: remove its miniature from the board and place it on the target's Character board, and the target gains 1 Contamination card on top of their Action discard pile. If they already have a Larva, the attacking one disappears, the existing one stays, and the Character still gains the Contamination card; this attack does not automatically kill them.
answers.evidence: 1. “Choose the target: the Intruder attacks a Character in its Room — with several Characters present, the one whose player has the FEWEST Action cards in hand; on a tie, the Character with the First Player token (or the next player in turn order).” 2. “For other Intruders, draw 1 Intruder Attack card: if it shows a symbol matching the attacking Intruder's type, resolve the card's effect; otherwise the attack misses. Ignore the blood icon during attacks.” 3. “Larva exception: draw no Attack card; use Infest below.” “Infest (Larva attack): a Larva does not draw Attack cards. Instead: remove the Larva miniature from the board and place it on the target's Character board (on the miniature picture), and the target gains 1 Contamination card. If the target already has a Larva, the attacking Larva disappears, the existing one stays, and the Character only gains the Contamination card; this attack does not automatically kill them (FAQ Rules 12).” “When a Character ‘gets a Contamination card,’ draw it from the Contamination deck and place it on top of their Action discard pile.”

requested_parts: Whether dressing a Serious Wound prevents death from another Wound at three Serious Wounds.
What happens on a third Light Wound.
What Heal removes.
Where the Corpse and Heavy Objects go upon death.
answers.answer: 1. No. Dressing ignores the card's effect but it still counts toward the three-wound limit, and dressing does not prevent death from a further Wound when there are already 3 Serious Wounds. 2. On a third Light Wound, clear the Light Wound track and suffer a Serious Wound. 3. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound card as the healing effect specifies. 4. On death, place a Character Corpse token in the Room and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: 1. “Dress a Serious Wound: flip the card face down — its effect is ignored, but it still counts toward the 3-wound limit. Dressing does not prevent death from a further Wound when you already have 3 Serious Wounds.” “A Character with 3 Serious Wounds dies instantly upon suffering ANY additional Wound (Light or Serious).” 2. “Light Wounds: track on your Character board — 1st marker on the upper space, 2nd on the lower space (= 2 Light Wounds); on a 3rd, clear the track and suffer a Serious Wound.” 3. “Heal: remove a Light Wound or discard a Dressed Serious Wound card, as the healing effect specifies.” 4. “Death: a Character with 3 Serious Wounds dies instantly upon suffering ANY additional Wound (Light or Serious). Remove the miniature, place a Character Corpse token in the Room (now a Character Corpse Object), and drop all their Heavy Objects there.”

requested_parts: Which cards Canteen/Shower scan and remove, and how they treat an Infected card with and without an existing Larva.
Which cards Surgery scans/removes and how it handles a Larva.
Surgery's cost, wound, passing, reshuffle, and hand consequences.
answers.answer: 1. Canteen/Shower scan all Contamination cards in the Character's hand and remove all scanned non-Infected cards from the game. If any scanned card is Infected, keep it; if there was no Larva before the scan, place a Larva on the Character board, while an already-present Larva means the Character dies and a Creeper is placed in the death Room. 2. Surgery scans all Contamination cards in the Action deck, hand, and discard pile, removes all Infected cards from the game, and removes a Larva from the Character board if present. 3. Surgery is a Room Action costing 2 Action cards; after it, suffer 1 Light Wound, automatically pass, and shuffle all cards (including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards) into the Action deck. The hand stays empty until next turn.
answers.evidence: 1. “For the optional Canteen/Shower hand scan, the complete outcome is below. Larva status means before this Room scan; the Infected rows apply when at least one scanned card is Infected.” Table: “Non-Infected | Remove the scanned non-Infected card from the game | No Larva from that result”; “Infected, no Larva already on board | Keep the Infected card | Place a Larva on Character board”; “Infected, Larva already on board | Keep the Infected card | Character dies; place 1 Creeper in the death Room.” 2. “Surgery — Scan ALL your Contamination cards (deck, hand, discard); remove all Infected ones; remove a Larva from your board if present.” “When a rule removes a Contamination card, remove it from the game.” 3. “Room Actions: Most Rooms grant a specific Action (see Player Reference). Cost: 2 Action cards.” “Surgery — Scan ALL your Contamination cards (deck, hand, discard); remove all Infected ones; remove a Larva from your board if present. Then suffer 1 Light Wound and automatically pass, shuffling all your cards (including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards) into your Action deck. Your hand stays empty until the next turn.”

requested_parts: Egg destruction from Shoot/Melee and Grenade.
Egg destruction from Molotov and Fire, including Vulnerability to Fire.
Egg Melee penalties or exceptions.
When Noise is rolled and where for remote attacks.
When the Nest is destroyed.
answers.answer: 1. Each Injury from Shoot or Melee destroys 1 uncarried Egg. A Grenade destroys 2 Eggs; uncarried Eggs allow the Nest Room to be targeted as if an Intruder were there. 2. A Molotov destroys 1 Egg immediately; its Fire marker can destroy Eggs during later Fire Damage steps. Fire normally destroys 1 uncarried Egg at each Event Phase Fire Damage step; with Vulnerability to Fire, the Nest Egg pool loses 2 per step. 3. A successful Egg Melee still draws 1 Contamination card onto the Action discard pile. A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound; the summary says the timing of the normal pre-roll draw relative to that miss exception is unspecified. 4. After every single Shoot, Melee, Grenade, or Molotov attempt to destroy an Egg, roll Noise, including on a miss. For a remote Grenade/Molotov, roll Noise in your own Room, not the Nest. 5. When no Eggs remain in the Nest (all carried away or destroyed), the Nest is destroyed and marked with 1 Injury marker.
answers.evidence: 1. “Shoot or Melee | Each Injury destroys 1 Egg. Resolve the normal attack, with the Egg Melee exception below.” “Grenade | Destroys 2 Eggs. Uncarried Eggs permit the Room to be targeted as if an Intruder were there.” 2. “Molotov Cocktail | Destroys 1 Egg immediately; its Fire marker can continue destroying Eggs in later Fire Damage steps.” “Fire marker | Normally destroys 1 uncarried Egg during every Event Phase Fire Damage step. For the Nest's Egg pool, Vulnerability to Fire increases this to 2 per step (FAQ Rooms 7).” 3. “Egg Melee penalties: a successful Egg Melee retains the normal draw of 1 Contamination card onto your Action discard pile. A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound. The manuals do not specify how to reconcile the normal pre-roll Contamination step with this miss exception; no refund or alternative draw timing is specified.” 4. “Noise after an attack attempt: after every single Shoot, Melee, Grenade or Molotov attempt to destroy an Egg, perform a Noise roll, including a miss. For a remote Grenade/Molotov, roll in your own Room, not the Nest (FAQ Rooms 2).” 5. “Egg tokens on the Intruder board represent the Eggs in the Nest; taking or destroying Eggs removes them from the Intruder board. When no Eggs remain (all carried away or destroyed), the Nest is destroyed — mark it with 1 Injury marker.”

requested_parts: Requirements and restrictions for entering a Pod, including what must be resolved before entry.
Pod capacity for Characters and Heavy Objects.
Immediate launch and its consequences.
Wait options, timing, and contingencies.
answers.answer: 1. The relevant Evacuation Section Room Action costs 2 Action cards. The Pod in that Section must be Unlocked and have a free Character space; entry is forbidden if the Section has an Intruder or Malfunction. Roll Noise first; if an Intruder appears or reaches the Section, entry fails. 2. Each Pod holds 2 Characters; Heavy Objects use no Character space. 3. After boarding, you may launch immediately: remove the Pod token and occupants' miniatures from the game; they stop participating, count as arriving on Earth, and still face the final Contamination and Objective checks. 4. Choosing to wait makes you pass the current turn while still treated as present in the Section for bag-development Noise rolls. If an Intruder appears in the Section, all Characters in Pods of that Section return to the Section Room. A new boarder may immediately launch both occupants. A Malfunction after boarding still permits waiting, launching, or exiting; it blocks only new entry. At the start of your first round in each later Player Phase, choose to wait and pass, launch, or exit free into the Section Room and take a full round of 2 Actions.
answers.evidence: 1. “Board: pay 2 Action cards for the corresponding Evacuation Section A/B Room Action. A Pod there must be Unlocked with a free Character space. No entry while the Section contains an Intruder or Malfunction. First roll Noise; an Intruder appearing or reaching the Section makes entry fail.” 2. “Capacity: 2 Characters per Pod. Heavy Objects take no Character space.” 3. “Launch immediately: after boarding you may launch. Remove the Pod token and its occupants' miniatures from the game; they stop participating and count as arriving on Earth. They still face the final Contamination and Objective checks.” 4. “Wait after boarding — complete waiting procedure: choosing to wait makes you pass the current turn, while you remain treated as present in the Section for bag-development Noise rolls (FAQ Rules 1). While waiting, apply all three contingencies: if an Intruder appears in the Section, every Character in any of its Pods immediately returns to the Section Room; if another Character boards your Pod, that new boarder may immediately launch both occupants; if a Malfunction appears, your normal wait/launch/exit choices remain available and only new entry is blocked. At the start of your first round in each later Player Phase, choose wait and pass, launch, or exit free into the Section Room and play a full round of 2 Actions (FAQ Rules 2–3).”

requested_parts: Order of endgame checks.
Result of two Damaged Engines.
Result of a non-Earth destination, including the Quarantine/Mars exception.
Contamination check for an infected survivor or one carrying a Larva, and whether Pod passengers undergo it.
answers.answer: 1. The order is Engines → Coordinates → Contamination → Objectives. 2. Two Damaged Engines make the ship explode; everything aboard dies, including hibernating Characters and Intruders, while launched Pod passengers are already away. 3.
